key_highlights: ASX logged an $80b post-US midterms relief rally ending the week higher, led by technology and data centre infrastructure while crude oil prices slumped.

Major retail department store David Jones collapsed into voluntary administration after landlord negotiations failed, triggering contagion concerns across retail REITs and consumer discretionary suppliers.
Banking sector faced headwinds as NAB shares slumped, driven by margin compression, elevated domestic inflation, and RBA hawkishness targeting higher unemployment.
Qantas faces a $1b fuel cost surge, cutting capacity and lifting airfares, while mining juniors and gold explorers see heavy equity capital raising activity.

sectors.trend: Robust junior exploration and gold capital raisings offset by commodity volatility.
sectors.implications: Strong investor appetite for gold and critical minerals exploration (e.g. BPM Minerals, Chalice Mining, Kuniko), but broader resource earnings hinge on Chinese demand and USD fluctuations.

sectors.trend: Divergence and margin pressure across majors; NAB posted sharp declines.
sectors.implications: Stagflation risks, RBA rate stickiness, and rising mortgage borrowing constraints pressure bank net interest margins and loan book quality across major lenders.

sectors.trend: Severe distress evidenced by David Jones entering voluntary administration.
sectors.implications: Major retail landlords (Scentre Group, Vicinity Centres) face occupancy and rent renegotiation risks; discretionary suppliers face bad debt write-offs and demand headwinds.

sectors.trend: Strong institutional inflow into cloud and data infrastructure despite private tech rationalisation.
sectors.implications: NextDC continues outperforming on structural data/AI demand, even as private tech counterparts like Canva restructure workforces.

sectors.trend: Airlines squeeze margins on fuel spikes; energy markets adjust to retreating crude prices.
sectors.implications: Qantas operational cuts and fare hikes illustrate input cost inflation, while alternative fuels (tallow/SAF) gain policy focus as crude softens.

key_themes: Global macro relief from US midterm results providing short-term tailwinds to broader equity indices (^AXJO)
Domestic consumer weakness culminating in tier-one retail insolvency (David Jones)
Persistent inflation and restrictive RBA stance depressing household borrowing and housing valuations
Divergent equity performances: high-conviction tech and precious metals thriving while credit and retail lag

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Commercial Real Estate & Retail Credit Contagion
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight retail REITs and consumer discretionary; monitor supplier provisioning and rental renegotiations.
Hedge exposure via defensive dividend aristocrats (healthcare, staples) and reduce leverage in banking portfolios.
Trim cyclical travel holdings; favour transport operators with robust hedging and dynamic pricing power.
Maintain diversified allocation in USD-earning multinationals and gold hedges.

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight digital infrastructure and data centre operators
opportunities.rationale: Sustained enterprise demand and capital rotation into secular growth assets insulated from consumer malaise.

opportunities.recommendation: Accumulate low-cost gold producers and well-funded exploration plays
opportunities.rationale: High institutional equity participation and gold price resilience against stagflation and geopolitical noise.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce exposure to retail REITs and discretionary retail suppliers
defensive_moves.rationale: Immediate counterparty insolvency risk and renegotiation overhang following David Jones's collapse.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Prune major bank holdings sensitive to loan book deterioration and margin compression
defensive_moves.rationale: NAB sell-off reflects sector margin pressure amid RBA hawkish bias and mortgage affordability drag.

market_outlook.short_term: Range-bound ASX 200 (^AXJO) trading between 8,100–8,350 as US midterm rally momentum meets domestic headwinds from retail insolvencies and bank margin compression.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautious 6–12 month outlook; earnings revisions across discretionary retail and banking will weigh on returns until RBA policy easing or housing stabilisation emerges.
key_catalysts: David Jones administrator reports and store closure announcements impacting retail REIT valuations
Upcoming RBA monetary policy statement and labor market data releases
Global crude oil trajectory and fuel surcharge flow-through to transport earnings
US legislative developments following the midterm shift
watch_list: Crude oil (Brent/WTI) and jet fuel crack spreads
Retail foot traffic and discretionary supplier payment default rates
